text: Lewis's argument from temporary intrinsics uses temporal parts to explain how:
choices: two objects can be composed of exactly the same simples at a time.
composition is restricted to objects whose parts constitute a life.
a persisting object can bear incompatible properties (being straight on Monday and bent on Tuesday) without contradiction, because distinct temporal parts bear the incompatible properties.
an object retains numerical identity precisely by having all of its parts essentially.
explanation: The temporary intrinsics problem is that one enduring thing seemingly has incompatible intrinsic properties (straight and bent); perdurantism resolves it by assigning straightness simpliciter to the Monday-stage and bentness simpliciter to the Tuesday-stage, which are distinct temporal parts. The other options describe unrelated mereological debates (coincidence, organicism, mereological essentialism).
